messages:
zoe: Quick sketch: instead of moving tenant slots directly, what if we introduce a transient 'shadow ledger' that records borrowed slot deltas during migration. This avoids immediate counter swaps and gives a single source-of-truth to reconcile. Thoughts?

kai: curious: is shadow ledger per-range or global per-node?

zoe: per-range ledger. Small object: {range, epoch, delta_in, delta_out, expires_at}. Nodes consult ledger when deciding eviction eligibility.

adar: does that change the eviction invariant? we still need 'tenant_residency <= reservation + active_shadow'.

zoe: exactly. eviction checks sum reservation + ledger.delta_in - ledger.delta_out. If negative, evict as usual.

nina: race scenario: two coordinators add conflicting ledgers for same range. How do we ensure idempotency?

zoe: ledger writes use CAS on range metadata (range_meta.version). write fails if version mismatch. We also include origin-id and monotonic epoch so duplicate offers are ignored.

kai: CAS is fine but what about partial application where one node applies delta_out and another node applies delta_in and no single ledger shows net 0?

zoe: ledgers are append-only records in the metadata store. We never mutate old ledger entries, we append a commit record once all participants ack. Consumer logic reads all ledger entries for range and computes net effect.

adar: append-only means we can replay, nice. How do we garbage collect old ledgers so they don't bloat metadata?

zoe: GC rule: epoch-based GC. Once range_meta.committed_epoch > ledger.epoch + GC_WINDOW we mark ledgers as tombstoned and sweep. GC_WINDOW default 3 epochs.

nina: pinned keys? pinned must not rely on ledger since pins are absolute. What if a pinned key is counted in delta_out by mistake?

zoe: pinned keys are excluded from ledger deltas. We keep separate pinned_count in metadata and migration refuses to proceed if pinned_count > threshold, or it takes an explicit pin-transfer step that sets pinned_proxy token.

kai: pinned_proxy token? how does that preserve semantics during short overlap?

zoe: token means both old and new owners check the proxy when resolving pin reads. The token expires after TTL and is recorded in metadata so recovery is possible.

adar: observability: want metrics: shadow_net_per_range, ledger_append_rate, pin_proxy_hits. Also trace id for each migration.

ops-bot: created ticket: MIG-2249 (add ledger metrics + tracing).

nina: performance: will adding ledger lookup on every eviction check add latency to the hot path?

zoe: we plan to cache computed ledger net for range in-memory with short TTL (100ms). Fast-path eviction uses cached net; miss triggers metadata fetch. Also many ranges won't be migrating simultaneously.

kai: what about node crash mid-migration? how do we avoid orphaned deltas that permanently inflate quotas?

zoe: we include expires_at and a conservative default TTL (5 minutes). After TTL, reconciler tries to recover by issuing compensating deltas: create reverse ledger entry and mark range for audit. If reconciler fails, alert.

adar: sounds plausible. Are compensating deltas always safe? could they double-evict?

zoe: compensating deltas are applied behind a maintenance flag and only when traffic is low OR after operator approval. Automatic compensating runs only when net ledger age > threshold and observed residency matches ledger effects.

nina: testing matrix? would love chaos tests where ledger entries are partially replicated and then nodes rejoin.

zoe: test plan: 1) unit tests for ledger aggregation, 2) staged chaos with single-range canary, 3) multi-range stress with mixed pin/prefill workloads, 4) leader failover during commit. We'll use synthetic traces + some sampled production traces.

kai: RPC change? we'll need a small header to carry range_epoch and trace_id so readers can short-circuit to cached ledger state.

zoe: yes new header: X-Range-Epoch (optional) and X-Ledger-Trace. Gate it behind feature flag. Backward compat: if header missing, nodes use pre-ledger logic.

adar: rollback story? if something goes wrong mid-rollback, how to ensure we don't leave tenants permanently penalized?

zoe: rollback sets a rollback_epoch marker in metadata and appends reversing ledgers for recent epochs. We treat rollback as a high-priority reconciler job. Also during rollback we increase TTL for pinned_proxy to avoid pin loss.

nina: alerting: page oncall if orphaned_shadow_count > 0 for 2m or if ledger_apply_error_rate > 1% over 5m.

ops-bot: added alert rules to staging config draft.

kai: one more: can we optimize by coalescing multiple small ledger entries into a single batch write? append-only still but batching reduces metadata store pressure.

zoe: yes batching is in plan. Batcher retains entries until flush_threshold or flush_interval. Batcher uses CAS on metadata to append atomically.

adar: I'm comfortable with this approach. It reduces coupling vs direct credit transfers. Keen to see sequence diagram and canary runbook.

zoe: will write short RFC with diagrams + ops runbook tonight. tagging @eng-sre for canary ops. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
